A request has client,id,fence,delta. Replays within retention return the original result; changed parameters conflict; stale fencing tokens reject at the protected receiver. Publish effect and dedup record together. Add an append-only local teaching journal with explicit crash points around record/effect publication, then replay recovery without claiming the in-memory anchor is durable.

independent_oracle: Enumerate client0..1, id1..3, delta-1..1, same/different payload, fence1..3 and every expiry boundary. Use a map of original requests/results plus a scalar high-water fence as the oracle. Attacker capability is replay/reorder or changing admitted request fields in this isolated original receiver; success is a synthetic counter change forbidden by the stated fence policy, or acceptance of conflicting intent. Repair and verify both rejection and unchanged effect. No real credentials, storage service or deployment is targeted.
